statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail returns to 12 in the low band after the Jackson Hole event resolved into an orderly close, while Stress stays elevated at 52 on the hawkish September repricing. The danger window is limited to the final thin Globex hour before the 21:00Z weekend halt.
recommendation: The only interval in this horizon in which any Nasdaq-100 venue is open is the 20:00Z-21:00Z Globex hour, where liquidity thins ahead of the weekend break. From 21:00Z no venue trades for the remainder of the 24-hour window, so conditional Tail settles at a weekend residual that reflects Sunday-reopen gap risk rather than any tradable price path.
headline: Session low holds through the closing auction and VIX finishes under Thursday's close, so Tail falls back to 12 and the low band, while a 12.8bp jump in the 2-year keeps Stress elevated at 52 into a dense macro week
body:
The event resolved. Chair Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote at 14:00Z reopened the September policy debate, and the price path that followed was the question this assessment has been tracking all afternoon. It answered in favour of orderly discovery. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 29,433.43, down 0.70%, inside a 29,383.92-29,752.78 range and roughly 50 points above a session low that was set around 17:00Z and then held for three consecutive hours, including through the closing auction. NQ futures print 29,486.75 with their own 29,436.75 low likewise intact. A market that stops making new lows, retraces, and then closes above the low is not producing the persistent no-retracement structure that Tail measures.

The volatility surface agrees. VIX finished at 14.40, down 0.11 on the day, off a 14.84 session high and below Thursday's 14.51 close. Implied volatility declining on a day that repriced the front end of the curve is a strong argument against a pathological path, and it is the main reason Tail steps down from 20 to 12 rather than holding in the watch band.

What is genuinely changed is the rates picture, and that belongs to Stress. The 2-year yield rose 12.8 basis points to 4.37%, the 5-year 9.2bp to 4.50% and the 10-year 5.4bp to 4.73%, against just 1.4bp on the 30-year. That bear-flattening is a clean expression of a shifted policy path: September rate-hike pricing moved from roughly 35% before the speech to above 50% after it. Gold fell sharply on the same impulse, which is consistent with a rates story rather than a growth scare.

The equity damage was rotational rather than broad. The Dow closed essentially flat at -0.02% and the S&P 500 at -0.25%, against the Nasdaq-100's -0.70%. Semiconductors carried the decline, with Marvell falling sharply after guiding to a weaker third-quarter gross-margin mix despite a revenue beat, while several large-cap non-semiconductor names finished higher. Breadth that splits this way normally reduces directional conviction and raises Stress; it does not supply the aligned one-way structure that would justify a higher Tail. Delayed cross-asset context confirms the same shape without contributing live price-path evidence.

Oil is not a factor. WTI closed at $83.38 and Brent at $88.25, both modestly lower, with no supply-disruption premium building.

For the horizon ahead, the constraint is mechanical. U.S. cash trading ended at 20:00Z and the CME weekend halt takes futures offline at 21:00Z, so 23 of the next 24 hours contain no open Nasdaq-100 venue at all. Conditional Tail settles at 8 to 10 across the weekend, a residual that covers headline accumulation into the Sunday 22:00Z reopen rather than any structure that could be traded. Confidence decays from 88 to 66 across the same span, entirely because the live evidence ages, not because it conflicts. Beyond this window the calendar turns dense: month-end on Monday, ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS on Tuesday, ADP and Broadcom earnings on Wednesday, ISM Services and claims on Thursday, and the August payrolls report on Friday.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours cover a full event cycle. Tail held between 11 and 14 with a mixed mode through Thursday's late session and the entire overnight, while Stress drifted from 48 up to 57 as the 14:00Z Jackson Hole keynote approached. Tail rose to 17 at 14:00Z as the speech printed and the first session low was set, eased to 14 at 15:00Z on an apparent recovery, then stepped to 20 at 16:00Z and 22 at 17:00Z when that recovery failed and price extended to a new low, with the mode turning to event/whipsaw and Stress peaking at 64. It eased to 20 at 18:00Z once the new low held and VIX slipped under Thursday's close, and stayed at 20 through 19:00Z into the closing auction. One hour, 10:00Z, has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The horizon has two phases and one transition. The current 20:00Z hour is the only one in which any Nasdaq-100 venue is open: U.S. cash has closed and a single thin Globex hour remains before the CME weekend halt, so the danger window is confined to 20:00Z-21:00Z and Tail sits at 12 in the low band. From 21:00Z no Nasdaq-100 venue trades for the rest of the window. Across those 23 closed hours conditional Tail settles at a weekend residual of 8 to 10 covering headline accumulation and Sunday-reopen gap risk rather than any tradable path, conditional Stress decays from 36 into the low band, and Confidence falls from 88 to 66 purely as the live evidence ages. The far-horizon values tick up marginally to reflect a lengthening unpriced news window ahead of the Sunday 22:00Z futures reopen, which falls beyond this horizon, and a week that carries month-end, ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS, ADP, Broadcom earnings, ISM Services and the August payrolls report.
